findings.title: IntoIter::drop double-free/UAF when an element's Drop panics
findings.evidence: In IntoIter::drop's drop_non_singleton (lines 2544-2554), the internal vec is moved out via mem::replace into a local `vec` (2546), its remaining elements are freed with ptr::drop_in_place(&mut vec[this.start..]) (2547), and only afterwards is the length neutralized with vec.set_len_non_singleton(0) (2548). If any element's destructor panics, unwinding skips set_len_non_singleton(0), so the local `vec` still has a nonzero length and its own Drop (ThinVec::drop, line 1910) runs drop_in_place over the same elements a second time, re-freeing already-freed memory (double free / use-after-free). Reachable from safe code: build a ThinVec<T> where T's Drop panics (e.g. thin_vec![T(1), T(2)]), call .into_iter(), and drop the IntoIter before fully consuming it (or let an element drop panic), then catch the unwind; std's vec::IntoIter avoids this with a DropGuard that deallocates without re-dropping. CVE-2026-6654 / RUSTSEC-2026-0103 (thin-vec <0.2.16).

findings.title: ThinVec::clear double-free/UAF when an element's Drop panics
findings.evidence: clear() (lines 1082-1086) frees its elements with ptr::drop_in_place(&mut self[..]) (1084) and only then resets the length with self.set_len(0) (1085). If an element's destructor panics, set_len(0) is never reached, so the ThinVec keeps a nonzero length; when the container is subsequently dropped, ThinVec::drop (1910) drop_in_place's the same slice again, re-freeing already-freed elements (double free / use-after-free). The std Vec::clear sets len to 0 *before* drop_in_place for exactly this reason. Reachable from safe code with a panicking Drop type: v.clear() inside catch_unwind, then drop v. CVE-2026-6654 / RUSTSEC-2026-0103 (thin-vec <0.2.16).
